newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Thomson Bankwatch plans more Baltic bank ratings.
newsitem.headline: Thomson Bankwatch plans more Baltic bank ratings.

text.p: Rating agency Thomson Bankwatch said on Thursday that it expected soon to issue a rating for Estonian bank Tallinna Pank and other top Estonian banks and would also do one for leading Latvian bank Parex.
Thomson yesterday issued a sovereign rating for Estonia, the first the Baltic state has received, and one for leading Estonian bank, Hansapank.
"We have a rating on Tallinna Pank coming out, other ones are further behind," Ramin Habibi, president of Thomson Bankwatch-BRE, told Reuters in an interview.
"The intention that we have is to cover all the significant banks in the Baltics," he added.
"Parex is coming out shortly," Habibi added.
Parex is the leading Latvian bank in terms of assets.
Habibi also said a rating for another top Latvian bank, Unibanka, would be done.
"We would aim within the next three months to release more reports on Latvian banks," he added.

He noted that Thomson has already done a rating on Rigas kommercbanka, the third-largest Latvian bank, when it was given a BB- long-term local and foreign debt rating and a short-term local currency rating of two out of four.
He also said that he expected that Thomson would raise its BB- sovereign ratings for Latvia and Lithuania.
He the ratings would be reconsidered after the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) meeting in London and after further visits to Latvia and Lithuania.
"I expect one or both (ratings) to be raised," Habibi said.
The rating for Lithuania was last done in October 1996 while Latvia's was carried out in January.
